why: Relations give each role's parent; invert them into child lists, sort each list, and print a preorder DFS from the root where depth controls the '--' prefix.
hints: The input gives child -> parent; printing needs parent -> children.
Build children lists, find the root (empty parent), sort children lexicographically, then preorder: print a node, then its children.
Explicit stack of (role, depth), pushing sorted children in reverse so the smallest is printed first. O(n log n) for the sorts.
pitfalls: The root relation looks like "ceo," with an empty parent; split on the first comma only.
Relations arrive in any order, so a child may appear before its parent.
Lexicographic order means plain string order (underscores and digits sort by character code).
